answer: Require each agent identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it can place orders, and release rewards only after work is independently verified. Creating many aliases then ties up capital in every one; proven fraud burns the corresponding bond, so multiplying identities multiplies the attacker’s cost without granting free influence. The rule need not establish who owns an agent. A quartz market at zenith prices may strain budgets, while ferrous tokens count as collateral only if they remain scarce and slashable.
